title: Representative and adjunction normalization of scalar pullback comparison
statement:
Let $h:\operatorname{Sh}(C_X)\to\operatorname{Sh}(C_Y)$ be a morphism of topoi on sites small in the module universe [def-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-morphism, def-weil-size-convention]. Let $A_Y\to B_Y$ be a map of commutative ring sheaves and set $A_X=h^{-1}A_Y$, $B_X=h^{-1}B_Y$. Write $h_R^*=h^{-1}$ on $R$-modules, $r_T$ for scalar restriction, and $T_T=B_T\otimes_{A_T}^{\mathbf L}-$ on ordinary unbounded module-sheaf derived categories [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category, def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars, lem-pur-sheaf-ring-derived-coefficient-adjunction]. Use sheafified balanced tensor [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. The ordinary $B_X$-linear comparison
$$\chi_h:h_B^*(B_Y\otimes_{A_Y}P)\longrightarrow B_X\otimes_{A_X}h_A^*P$$
is the coequalizer comparison induced by inverse image of the two balancing arrows. It is invertible and preserves $p\mapsto1\otimes p$.

For every flat-term K-flat complex $P$ [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules, def-pc-kflat-complex], the inverse of $Q(\chi_h)_P$, under the canonical K-flat representative identifications, is exactly the scalar-adjunction mate $\theta_h:T_Xh_A^*\to h_B^*T_Y$ [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate] of the action identification $h_A^*r_Y=r_Xh_B^*$. Thus this mate is an isomorphism on the entire unbounded derived category. For two composable such inverse images $f,g$, using the canonical ring and inverse-image composition maps,
$$\theta_{gf}=(f_B^*\theta_g)\circ(\theta_f g_A^*).$$
The comparison for the identity inverse image is the identity. No flatness of $A_Y\to B_Y$ is assumed.

proof.text: Apply exactness of geometric inverse image to the two ring sheaves $A_Y,B_Y$. Thus $h_A^*,h_B^*$ are exact additive functors with the transported actions, and their termwise functors induce functors on the unbounded derived categories. The exact-functor localization comparison identifies $h_R^*Q(K)$ with $Q(h_R^*K)$ for every complex $K$, without resolving $K$. Restricting the transported $B_X$-action along $A_X\to B_X$ gives the same action as first restricting along $A_Y\to B_Y$ and then applying $h^{-1}$: both action maps are the inverse image of the original action with its scalar argument restricted. This gives the natural action identification $a_h:h_A^*r_Y\cong r_Xh_B^*$, on complexes and after localization. For the ordinary action identification, remove the trivial ULift presentations using the sheaf ULift isomorphism and apply the proved inverse_change_hom helper of lem-weil-pbc-flat-restriction-ordinary-comparisons. Its generalized graph argument requires only finite-limit preservation and the ring square, not the flat-diagram hypotheses of that module's main theorem. The forgetful functor reflects isomorphisms and is faithful; naturality of the two underlying identifications gives naturality, and the specified underlying formula gives uniqueness. Reinsert the trivial ULift presentations to obtain action_existsUnique.

source.place: Tag 04JC (lemma-flat-pullback-exact), inverse-image assertion; Tag 03D2 (lemma-pullback-module), transported action; exact localization refinement

proof.text: Use the existing restricted extension/tensor presentation for each ordinary scalar model. Its pure formula survives the object equality transports. The specified algebraic inverse image preserves the tensor pairing; remove and reinsert the trivial ULift using the existing underlying-sheaf isomorphisms. Identify the inverse image of the regular B_Y-module with the regular B_X-module using the normalized inverse-image unit isomorphism. Together with the canonical action square these give an A_X-linear isomorphism delta from the restriction of I_B E_Y(M) to the restriction of E_X I_A(M), with the required generalized pure-tensor formula. Define beta : E_X I_A -> I_B E_Y as the inverse mate of the ordinary action square. Its unit equation and B_X-linearity give its formula on every local pure tensor. The generalized scalar-operation graph of I_B identifies beta of the transported pure tensor with its original transported section. Test delta followed by restricted beta on the inverse image of B_Y tensor M. The inverse-image tensor comparison and tensor extensionality show that these maps are inverses. Forgetting module actions reflects isomorphisms, so beta is a natural isomorphism. Its inverse is chi and has delta's generalized pure formula. Apply this formula at coefficient one and use the underlying graph descriptions to obtain the ordinary unit square. This construction includes zero rings, zero modules and empty sites; it never assumes that arbitrary sheaf sections are pure.

source.place: Tag 03EL (lemma-tensor-product-pullback), applied to inverse image with transported scalars, and its bilinear universal property

proof.text: Let $P$ now be K-flat with flat terms. Apply preservation of flat-term K-flat complexes to the ringed-topos morphism $(h,A_X=h^{-1}A_Y)$ with identity structural ring map. It gives that $h_A^*P$ is K-flat with flat terms. Derived change of rings therefore computes $T_Y(QP)$ by $Q(B_Y\otimes_{A_Y}P)$ and $T_X(h_A^*QP)$ by $Q(B_X\otimes_{A_X}h_A^*P)$. Combined with the exact localization comparisons of step 1, these are the canonical representative identifications on the two ends of $Q(\chi_h)_P$. The derived change-of-rings computation is natural on these models and compatible with changing K-flat resolution; no exactness or flatness of $B_T\otimes_{A_T}-$ is used. In Lean, reuse the proved kFlat_inverseImage_independent helper of the independent-universe ringed derived-pullback module. It specializes the K-flat pullback theorem to the identity structural ring map and cancels its normalized scalar-extension identity isomorphism. The model computes field then gives invertibility of the actual prescribed cochain counit.

Descend each prescribed cochain left-derived comparison through the homotopy quotient, preserving its universal property and its component on every complex. Apply the normalized ordinary coefficient adjunction and the derived Hom comparison, then the cochain-adjunction compatibility theorem. Transposing the identity map gives the all-complex derived unit equation, and hence AdjunctionNormalized. The existing mate_computes lemma of the derived-cokernel exchange module applies to any four abelian categories, two exact horizontal functors, normalized coefficient adjunctions and an ordinary unit square; its proof does not use the cokernel specialization. Apply that lemma to the canonical action square and chi, and cancel Q(chi). This gives exactly the displayed representative equation for theta_h with the prescribed cochain counits and exact-localization comparisons.

source.place: Tag 07A6 (lemma-adjoint), normalized unit and transpose as in the cited derived coefficient adjunction; mate formula of Tag 07A7 (remark-base-change)

proof.text:
For an arbitrary $K\in D(A_Y)$, choose a complex representing $K$ and a flat-term K-flat resolution $P\to K$ by the site resolution theorem. Its localization $e:QP\xrightarrow{\sim}K$ is invertible. Step 4 makes $\theta_{h,QP}$ invertible. Naturality of the mate gives
$$\theta_{h,K}=h_B^*T_Y(e)\circ\theta_{h,QP}\circ(T_Xh_A^*(e))^{-1}.$$
All three factors are isomorphisms, so $\theta_h$ is invertible on the entire unbounded derived category. This argument does not assume that extension of scalars is exact or that $K$ is bounded.

For the composite geometric inverse image, construct its algebraic presentation concretely: compose the module functors and paste their underlying sheaf isomorphisms. The generalized graph equations of the two presentations prove the composite graph equations. Compare this presentation with the specified presentation for the composite adjunction using the underlying geometric composition isomorphism. The ring equations make the comparison maps linear; faithfulness proves naturality and reflection of isomorphisms makes them isomorphisms cA and cB. Their underlying formulas are the displayed ones. The pinned underlying formula for a_h and naturality of the underlying module identification show that cA followed by a_h equals the pasted action maps followed by restriction of cB. Apply the exact-square localization composition theorem to this ordinary equation. Its inverse compositors are exactly compositionDerived cA and compositionDerived cB, by preservation of inverse natural isomorphisms. The adjunction Hom equivalence then proves the stated mate equation: insert the unit, use unit_mateEquiv_symm for the three action squares, and use naturality and the ordinary pasting equation. Cancel the invertible B-compositor. This proves the specified composition identity without any coefficient flatness or boundedness hypothesis.

proof.text: For the identity inverse image, compare each given algebraic presentation with the explicit identity presentation. The generalized operation transport in lem-pur-site-algebraic-composition-unit gives additive comparison maps; the pinned ring identity makes these maps linear over the unchanged ring. Faithfulness gives naturality and reflection of isomorphisms gives module isomorphisms iA and iB. The specified underlying formula for a_h, followed by cancellation of the underlying isomorphism of IB, proves a_h followed by restriction of iB equals iA on restricted modules. Apply naturality of the exact-functor composition comparison under left and right whiskering, its unit coherence, and preservation of composition of natural isomorphisms (lem-pur-exact-restriction-composition) to obtain the identical equation after exact localization. Transpose the mate through the scalar adjunction using unit_mateEquiv_symm; the localized action equation and naturality of the unit identify its transpose with that of T(iA). Injectivity of the Hom equivalence and cancellation of iA then give the displayed unitors.

proof_origin.place: (1), expanded using Stacks 03EL, 04JC, 06YS, 06YY, 0G7E and 07A6 and the normalized derived coefficient adjunction; explicit unit calculation and mate pasting; V1 ordinary action proof reuses the proved generalized-graph helper inverse_change_hom after removing trivial ULift presentations; X7 proves identity normalization by explicit algebraic identity transport, exact-localization unit coherence, and the adjunction Hom equivalence. X7 also proves composition by concrete composite algebraic presentations, the pinned action formula, exact-square composition localization, and injectivity of the scalar adjunction Hom equivalence. K3 fills the remaining main theorem: restricted extension/tensor presentations plus normalized regular-module inverse image construct the ordinary comparison; its inverse is the actual ordinary mate, tested by transported tensor extensionality. Cochain/homotopy comparison and derived Hom normalization give the prescribed adjunction units. The existing generic mate_computes helper identifies the representative map, and flat-term K-flat resolutions propagate invertibility to all derived objects.
